core_obligations: Build the first map by composing the map from A into the double localisation with the universal property of the localisation at S', landing in the localisation at the product set (proof lines 1499-1501).
Apply the universal property a second time, since the elements of the image of S are invertible, to obtain a map out of the localisation at that image (proof lines 1501-1504).
Build the map in the opposite direction by the same two applications of the universal property and note that the two are inverse to each other (proof lines 1506-1512).
proof_roadmap: Get one map by applying the universal property twice (proof lines 1498-1504).
Get the other map the same way and observe the compositions are identities (proof lines 1506-1513).
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that for multiplicative subsets S and S' of a ring A, the localisation at the product set is isomorphic to the localisation of the localisation at S' at the image of S (statement lines 1492-1496). Unlike the module version of the same phenomenon, the proof does not construct the two maps on fractions: it obtains each of them by applying the universal property of the localisation twice, first to the composite map from A and then again because the relevant elements become invertible, and checks that the two are inverse by the same mechanism (proof lines 1498-1513). Recognising that the universal property is available here, where for modules it is not yet established, is what determines the shape of the argument. H2.
